messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT (INC-2026-073) -> p99 generation latency spike detected in us-west-2 hosted-rt cluster. Threshold breached: p99 > 2.5s. Potential root: KV cache pressure / fragmentation. Paging oncall: @alex @jamie @priya. Dashboard: https://internal.metrics/redwood/INC-2026-073 :rotating_light:

alex: I see streaming stalls, clients report timeout-ish behavior. p95 ~ 250ms but p99 jumping to 2.6-3.2s on models that rely on large prefill + KV reuse. Logs show a lot of blocking tasks while waiting for KV fetches.

jamie: eviction rate spiked 4x starting 10:10 UTC, prefill-to-decode ratio abnormal (prefill ops >> decode ops). KV memory usage % not super high (~82%) but fragmentation metric 'kv_frag_ratio' at 0.68 (normally 0.2-0.3). Suspect fragmentation + odd prefill pattern causing OOM-ish pauses when internal GC/compaction runs.

priya: reproducing locally on canary with load test. prefill threads queue up, then some worker threads block on disk-backed pages while others finish decode. Streaming stalls correspond to the blocked prefill queue.

alex: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) disable proactive prefill for high-length prompts (toggle), 2) temporarily raise eviction threshold to prefer quick LRU evictions (less compaction), 3) route affected tenants to smaller-seq-length model variant that doesn't prefill as aggressively. Which are realistic to flip now?

jamie: 1) toggle prefill is config flag: `runtime.prefill.enabled=false` per model-route. Low-risk. 2) eviction tuning requires restart of a subset of runtime pods to pick up new config (rolling). Doable but will cause brief reconns. 3) routing fallback we can enable via smart-routing: set policy `route_on_latency=true` and add fallback model id `redwood-rt-smallseq-v1`.

priya: I'm running the prefill toggle on canary route now to validate. If streaming stalls improve we'll roll to prod.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started rollout of config patch `prefill-toggle-canary` to 3 pods (pod ids: serve-rt-7b9, serve-rt-8c0, serve-rt-9d1). Link: https://deploys/internal/1234

alex: note: customer A is hitting p99 errors and reported degraded UX on long chat sessions. CS escalation in #customer-success — @santiago will coordinate comms.

santiago: pinged CS lead, told them we're toggling prefill canary and will update in 15m. No data exfil or request loss, just higher latency and stalls.

(priya posts quick results) priya: canary prefill disabled -> p99 on canary down from 3.0s to 420ms under similar load. Streaming stalls gone for that subset. Looks promising.

alex: plan: 1) roll prefill toggle to 50% of runtime pods (non-disruptive), 2) enable routing fallback for top 10% noisy tenants, 3) start eviction compaction job (lower priority) to defrag KV in background, 4) collect traces for the paused workers. Who owns each?

jamie: I'll do the rollout and routing changes. I'll leave a short note in the rollout message about expected transient reconnects.

priya: I'll kick off the background compaction job and provide progress updates. Command I used locally: 
```
# start compaction job (example)
kubectl -n serving exec job/kv-compactor -- /bin/sh -c "python compactor.py --shards 0-31 --mode=background --throttle=0.2"
```

melissa: I'm on the next shift in ~25m. Alex handing off; will keep monitoring.

alex: handing off to melissa. Key context: prefill toggle is the primary mitigation, routing fallback enabled for several heavy tenants, compaction job running. Customer A paged but not asking for rollback. Logs/traces saved under /traces/INC-2026-073.

melissa: ack taking over. I'll watch p99, streaming error rates, and the compactor logs. Please drop any ongoing experiment links here.

ops-bot: rollout `prefill-toggle-50pct` initiated by jamie at 10:35 UTC. Affected pods: serve-rt-*-grp1. Rollout progress: 0/24 -> 12/24 -> 24/24. No immediate 5xx spike detected.

jamie: routing fallback applied for tenants [cust-A, cust-7, cust-13] using `redwood-rt-smallseq-v1`. Observe warm-up latency will be slightly higher but avoids prefill-heavy path.

melissa: after handoff quick checks: p99 across cluster down from peak 3.2s -> 480ms over 20m. Streaming stall events down 90%. Still seeing some tail outliers (p99 ~ 700-900ms) for a few pods; suspect compaction still running.

alex: items for follow-up (post-incident): - Investigate why prefill vs decode imbalance occurred (recent traffic shift? regression). - Add a safeguard: if eviction fragmentation > 0.5 trigger auto-toggle prefill or auto-route fallback. - Improve observability: per-route kv_fragment_ratio and per-tenant prefill/decode counters.

priya: added a tracking ticket: https://internal.tracker/RED-8723 "kv fragmentation auto-mitigation". Tests to reproduce and unit for compactor.

melissa: I'm updating incident timeline and will coordinate postmortem. Who should write blameless summary? alex/jamie + priya preferable.

alex: I'll draft timeline. jamie take the mitigation steps writeup. priya compaction and reproduction notes. melissa will own postmortem doc.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-073 status: Mitigated (partial) at 10:55 UTC — p99 restored within SLO for majority; monitoring watch until full compaction complete.

melissa: closing handoff: I'll follow up with a PM/infra sync tomorrow to discuss permanent config and SLO guardrails. Leaving channel open for 1h for any regressions.

oncall-bot: Note: next on-call rotation reminder scheduled for 11:00 UTC.

alex: thanks team :thumbsup: great coordination.

(End of thread)
